plain: To pass on information or a quality

webster.text: To give, grant or communicate; to bestow on another a share or portion of something; as, to impart a portion of provisions to the poor.

example.quote: He is to regulate all intercourse with foreign powers, and it is his duty to impart to the Senate every material intelligence he receives.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 4, North Carolina Convention, Mr. IREDELL, July 28, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
